finding.title: Type and log the swallowed catch blocks in content_database.dart, seed_manager.dart, and DeviceAccountX

evidence.quote:
} catch (_) {
            // no-op: CREATE IF NOT EXISTS is defensive; failure here is non-fatal

} catch (_) {
            // no-op: ALTER TABLE fails if column already exists (prior upgrade path); non-fatal

finding.why: content_database.dart's 4 migration catches use untyped `catch (_)` with only a comment, no AppLogger call — if an ALTER/CREATE fails for a real reason (disk full, corrupt file) rather than the anticipated 'already exists' case, the content DB silently proceeds on a half-migrated schema with zero diagnostic trail; contrast with ContentDbHealthChecker in this same batch, which does this correctly with typed `on SqliteException catch (e, st)` plus logger calls, but never gets a chance to react because no exception escapes here. seed_manager.dart's _rollback() catch(_) is a log-less outlier inside a file where every other catch (_extractSeedDb, _atomicReplace, _readSchemaVersion, _readInstalledVersion, _stampInstalledVersion) does call _logger?.error — a reader following this file's own dominant convention would log here too. DeviceAccountX.accountTier catches ArgumentError, an Error subtype EH-4 explicitly says never to catch (Errors are meant to crash loudly on programming bugs); here a malformed/legacy tier string in the DB silently downgrades to AccountTier.local with no signal that stored data is bad.
finding.recommendation: Give the content_database.dart and seed_manager.dart catches typed `on SqliteException`/`on Exception` clauses plus an AppLogger call (matching content_db_health_checker.dart's pattern). Change AccountTier.fromStorageKey to expose a non-throwing tryFromStorageKey returning null (or throw a non-Error type) so accountTier doesn't catch Error.
acceptance_criteria: No catch block in these 3 files is both untyped and log-less; EH-3's Pending tightened log-less-catch checker returns zero for them.
DeviceAccountX.accountTier no longer catches an Error subtype (EH-4's Pending avoid_catching_errors).

finding.title: Use `is TalkerDioLogger` instead of a runtimeType.toString() string match in dio_client_test.dart
finding.why: Comparing runtimeType.toString() to a string literal bypasses the type system: a rename or a subclass would silently break or falsely pass this check with a confusing failure message, where `is TalkerDioLogger` (talker_dio_logger is already a transitive dependency of tool/lib/dio_client.dart) is both safer and clearer.
finding.recommendation: Import package:talker_dio_logger/talker_dio_logger.dart and replace the check with `dio.interceptors.any((i) => i is TalkerDioLogger)`.
acceptance_criteria: Test uses an `is` type check, no runtimeType.toString() comparison remains, test still passes

finding.title: Relocate test/core/streak/*_test.dart to mirror lib/features/gamification/streak/ (AG-5)
finding.why: Commit 92125f82 ('refactor(W2.22): promote core/streak/ -> features/gamification/streak/', 20 May 2026) moved all 5 streak source files out of core/, but left both test files behind at test/core/streak/. AG-5 requires lib/a/b/foo.dart <-> test/a/b/foo_test.dart. A contributor working on lib/features/gamification/streak/ who checks test/features/gamification/streak/ (as AG-5 promises) finds nothing, risking duplicate tests or a false 'no coverage' assumption for a module that actually has 305 lines of tests, including two named D17 regression tests.
finding.recommendation: git mv both files to test/features/gamification/streak/{streak_event_test.dart,streak_state_provider_test.dart}. Note the new location is one directory level deeper, so streak_state_provider_test.dart's helper import must change from '../../helpers/drift_memory.dart' to '../../../helpers/drift_memory.dart'. Verify `flutter test test/features/gamification/streak/` is green and delete the now-empty test/core/streak/ dir.
acceptance_criteria: test/core/streak/ no longer exists; both suites pass unchanged at test/features/gamification/streak/.
The [Pending] AG-5 unmirrored-test-file audit check referenced at docs/coding-standards.md:523, once implemented, reports zero violations for this module.

finding.title: Show user-facing error feedback on the StateError path in TutoredChildrenSection._fireEntryPullAndNavigate
finding.why: The permissionDenied and error branches of the preceding switch both show a ScaffoldMessenger snackbar so the user learns why they didn't land in the talmid view. The `on StateError catch` block three lines later only logs via AppLogger and calls exit()+dismissLoading() — no snackbar, no dialog. If buildTutoredPullServiceFromWidget throws (documented as the 'non-cloud accounts' case), the user taps a tutored-child row, watches the loading spinner, and it disappears with zero explanation — indistinguishable from a silent hang.
finding.recommendation: Add the same ScaffoldMessenger snackbar pattern (with an AppLocalizations-backed message) to the StateError catch block.
acceptance_criteria: A widget test stubs the pull service to throw StateError and asserts a SnackBar/error message appears
The StateError catch block gives feedback consistent with the permissionDenied/error branches

finding.title: Resolve outboxProcessor lazily in syncOrchestratorProvider instead of capturing it by value
finding.rule: SM-6 lazy-resolver consistency / Nygard-lens: stale capture across DB swap
finding.why: Every other volatile build-time dependency in this same constructor call (gateway, merge router, outbox DAO, identity status) is deliberately passed as a lazy `() => ref.read(...)` resolver specifically — per the inline comments at lines 136-137, 161-163 — 'so a DB swap (multi-account flow) is picked up without rebuilding the orchestrator singleton.' outboxProcessor is the one exception: it's read once (line 129) and stored as a plain value field. outboxProcessorProvider (outbox_providers.dart) watches userDatabaseProvider and rebuilds on a DB swap; database_provider.dart confirms userDatabaseProvider swaps via the independently-mutable accountDbFileNameProvider, decoupled from authStateProvider (the only thing syncOrchestratorProvider itself watches). If a DB swap can occur without authStateProvider's watched value also changing in the same tick, the orchestrator keeps draining through an OutboxProcessor bound to the pre-swap, superseded UserDatabase/outboxDao while its other lazily-resolved collaborators (gateway, merge router) may already be pointing at the new account — a split-identity state. Confirming this needs tracing whether the app's account-switch flow (account_actions.dart) can complete a DB swap before authStateProvider's emitted value settles to the new account.
finding.recommendation: Change the outboxProcessor parameter to a lazy `resolveOutboxProcessor: () => ref.read(outboxProcessorProvider)` resolver, matching resolveGateway/resolveMergeRouter/resolveOutboxDao, so it can't go stale relative to its siblings.
acceptance_criteria: syncOrchestratorProvider resolves outboxProcessor via a lazy resolver rather than a captured value.

Regression/integration test: trigger a userDatabaseProvider swap while syncOrchestratorProvider stays alive (authState unchanged) and assert the next drain operates against the new outboxDao's pending rows, not the pre-swap instance.
